title: The Mini's revolutionary technical choices
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The Mini became revolutionary by combining transverse engine, front-wheel drive, corner wheels and a cabin-led layout.
content:
The Mini was not revolutionary simply because it was small. It became important because it combined several technical choices in a very short body and made them work as one system.

Packaging before appearance

The A-Series engine was mounted transversely at the front, with the gearbox below it. Front-wheel drive removed the need for a propshaft to the rear. The wheels were placed near the corners to open the space between them.

These decisions gave the Mini a cabin far larger than its exterior length suggested. The main performance was not speed, but the ratio between space used by passengers and space occupied on the road.

Handling from compactness

The Mini felt lively because it was light, wide for its size and short. Its modest power mattered less than its layout. That same structure later made the Cooper versions and rally successes credible.

The model's birth is covered in why the Mini was created. Motorsport follows in why the Mini worked in rallying.
